proposed_from.topic: Extend the adaptive estimation method for TRAE in https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01337 to allow misspecification error, borrowing insights from the DeepIV misspecification analysis in https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04236.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: {"published_axis":"The closest result is TanSyrgkanis2026Adaptive, Theorem 3.13, which gives adaptive TRAE rates only under realizability and exact critic closeness. The proposed theorem makes critic blindness a distinct population error and proves a termination-compatible discrepancy-path bound for TRAE.","repo_axis":"The nearest archived proposal is stat_npiv_nosol_modulus/source_representer_minimax. seed_details.kernel: A discrepancy-selected TRAE path has a uniform weak- and strong-metric oracle inequality with separately defined target approximation and witness-blindness errors.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Tan and Syrgkanis because Remark 3.8 says to add approximation error to the noise.
seed_details.rebuttal: The remark neither defines a critic-orthogonal population defect nor proves termination or strong error for implicit-operator minimax estimation.

seed_details.kernel: A diagonal NPIV lower bound determines whether critic-orthogonal residual error is necessarily amplified by inverse regularization.
seed_details.red_team: Dikkala et al. already allow approximate witnesses.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their upper bound does not identify the minimax price of a discrepancy-selected TRAE path under separate target and witness defects.

seed_details.kernel: A split-sample selector jointly chooses target class, witness class, and discrepancy threshold at the best candidate oracle rate without known approximation radii.
seed_details.red_team: Validation-based RDIV model selection already supplies the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: RDIV validates an explicit learned-operator loss; it cannot detect residual components omitted by an adversarial witness.

seed_details.kernel: A cross-fitted, adaptively tuned primal-dual TRAE estimator has a misspecification-aware linear expansion and bias-aware confidence interval for a linear causal functional.
seed_details.red_team: Ai and Chen already provide misspecified conditional-moment inference.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their pseudo-true expansion does not control adaptive primal and dual inverse regularization or critic-blind residual drift.

seed_details.kernel: For a fixed approximation neighborhood, characterize the critical misspecification radius at which a TRAE-based confidence interval for a linear functional must include zero.
seed_details.red_team: Approximate-moment sensitivity intervals already solve this.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existing intervals do not incorporate source-condition inverse amplification or data-adaptive adversarial nuisances.

seed_details.kernel: Derive an observable frontier at which explicit-operator RDIV and implicit-operator TRAE cease to be asymptotically equivalent under operator and witness approximation.
seed_details.red_team: The estimators have different losses, so non-equivalence is unsurprising.
seed_details.rebuttal: A derived frontier could separate operator-learning error from critic deficiency, but the observable primitive is presently unclear.

seed_details.kernel: Define a witness-deficiency radius and derive the critical radius at which adaptive TRAE loses its realizable strong-metric order.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely a restatement of a finite witness class.
seed_details.rebuttal: The focal object is a population residual-direction deficiency with an inverse-problem phase transition, not witness dimension.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize the semiparametric efficiency bound for a pseudo-true linear functional in a misspecified inverse conditional-moment model and test whether adaptive TRAE attains it.
seed_details.red_team: This is conventional semiparametric misspecification theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: The inverse operator and source-conditioned primal-dual restriction change the tangent geometry, but attainment by TRAE is presently too uncertain.

proposed_from.literature_map: Tan and Syrgkanis establish smoothness-adaptive TRAE under target realizability and exact witness closeness; their Remark 3.8 explicitly leaves approximation error for the discrepancy noise untreated. Li et al. provide misspecified RDIV decomposition and validation selection with an explicit learned conditional operator. Dikkala et al. supply the localized-Rademacher minimax geometry and benchmark witness approximation. Bennett et al. relax closedness for minimax IV but retain realizability. The M16 screen found no policy-value target in the anchored TRAE setup, and the M17 screen found no assignment or sampling symmetry capable of generating a counterfactual permutation orbit.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:common-audit-oracle / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The oracle inequality is conditional on the attained minimum-norm least-squares inverse target h^dagger and does not assert that the misspecified conditional moment has a causal structural solution.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline is an oracle inequality for h^dagger under ass:pseudotrue-attainment; it targets h_0 only on the additional ass:iv-validity and ass:completeness branch.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: prop:zero-defect-reduction / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The optimized power reduction is asserted only when s_{k_0,n} is at most one and the finite grid reaches the displayed oracle scale.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Outside that regime the result is only the clipped bound ||hhat-h^dagger||_2^2 <= 4B^2.

banked_reason: Sound negative result for a note-defined common-audit TRAE hybrid, but below the field novelty floor because no published TRAE or DeepIV workflow uses the exact refuted architecture.
